app.photos.collections.add_title.note: Title of the list that opens from the selection bar's Add to collection: the collections to add the selected photos to, and New collection…. {count} is how many photos and videos are selected.

app.photos.collections.delete.note: Button that deletes the collection open in Images (its photos stay): in the bar over its photos (a button, or the screen-reader name of a bin icon on a narrow screen), and the confirming button of app.photos.collections.delete_title.

app.photos.collections.delete_message.note: Under the title of the confirmation asked before deleting a collection (app.photos.collections.delete_title): deleting it doesn't delete its photos and videos.

app.photos.collections.delete_title.note: Title of the confirmation asked before deleting the collection open in Images. {name} is its name. Only the collection goes; its photos stay (app.photos.collections.delete_message). Buttons: Delete collection and Cancel.

app.photos.collections.name_placeholder.note: Placeholder of the field for a collection's name, when making a new collection or renaming one.

app.photos.collections.new_item.note: Last item of the list that opens from the selection bar's Add to collection: makes a new collection (asks for its name) with the selected photos.

text.one: {count} picture will be added to it.
text.other: {count} pictures will be added to it.

app.photos.collections.new_message.note: In the box that asks for a new collection's name, under its title: the selected photos go into the new collection. {count} is how many photos and videos are selected.

app.photos.collections.new_title.note: Title of the box that asks for a new collection's name, made from the selected photos.

app.photos.collections.pictures.note: Under a collection's name in the list of collections opened from Images' Collections button: how many photos and videos it holds.

app.photos.collections.remove_needs_upda.text: Your device needs an update to remove photos from a collection.
app.photos.collections.remove_needs_upda.note: Title of the message shown when Remove from collection (app.shell.remove_from_collection) is tapped and the device's software is older than that feature. The account that set the device up gets an Update button under it (common.update) that starts the device's update; others get app.shell.device_update.ask_owner.

app.photos.collections.rename.note: Title of the box that renames the collection open in Images, and the screen-reader name of the pencil beside its name (and of a tap on its name) that opens that box.

app.photos.collections.sheet_empty.text: No collections yet — select some pictures and choose Add to collection.
app.photos.collections.sheet_empty.note: In the list of collections opened from Images' Collections button (on a phone held upright) when there is none. Add to collection is the name of the selection bar's item (app.shell.add_to_collection): use the same words.

app.photos.collections.sort_name.note: In Collections' Sort by menu: by name, A to Z.

app.photos.collections.sort_newest.note: In Collections' Sort by menu: the collections made most recently first (the default).

app.photos.copies.all.note: Button of the confirmation app.photos.copies.single_text: deletes every copy of the photo or video from the device, in every folder (also from computers and phones that sync those folders). {count} is how many copies: always 2 or more, so both forms are the plural.

app.photos.copies.every.note: Button of the confirmation app.photos.copies.several_text: deletes the selected photos and videos and every other copy of them on the device, in every folder (also from computers and phones that sync those folders).

app.photos.copies.only_these.note: Button of the confirmation app.photos.copies.several_text: deletes only the selected photos and videos (the copies shown in Images); their other copies stay on the device.

app.photos.copies.only_this.note: Button of the confirmation app.photos.copies.single_text: deletes only the copy shown in Images (the one this photo or video was opened from). The other copies stay on the device, and Images goes on showing the picture at one of them.

text.one: {count} of them also has copies elsewhere on your device. Delete only these copies, or every copy? This can't be undone.
text.other: {count} of them also have copies elsewhere on your device. Delete only these copies, or every copy? This can't be undone.

app.photos.copies.several_text.note: Text of the confirmation asked before deleting several selected photos and videos in Images (the selection bar's Delete) when some of them are also stored as other copies on the device, under the title app.photos.selection.delete_title. Copies are the same picture stored at more than one path on the device: in another folder, or downloaded to a phone or computer and synced back. Images shows it once. {count} is how many of the selected items have other copies (1 or more, at most all of them). "These copies" are the selected items themselves. Buttons: app.photos.copies.only_these, app.photos.copies.every and Cancel. The web say the same (web.images.copies.several_text).

text.one: There are {count} copies of it on your device. Delete only this copy, or all of them? This can't be undone.
text.other: There are {count} copies of it on your device. Delete only this copy, or all of them? This can't be undone.

app.photos.copies.single_text.note: Text of the confirmation asked before deleting one photo or video in Images that the device holds as several copies (the viewer's Delete, or the selection bar's Delete with one item selected), under the title app.photos.viewer.delete_title (or app.photos.viewer.delete_video_title) or app.photos.selection.delete_title. Copies are the same picture stored at more than one path on the device: in another folder, or downloaded to a phone or computer and synced back. Images shows it once. {count} is how many copies there are, this one included: always 2 or more, so both forms are the plural. "It" is the photo or video named in the title: word it to fit either (the copies can carry the gender). Buttons: app.photos.copies.only_this, app.photos.copies.all and Cancel. The web say the same (web.images.copies.single_text).

app.photos.grid.collection_items_span.note: Under an open collection's name, over its photos in Images: how many photos and videos it holds, then the months they span (app.photos.months.short_title, range_in_year or range). Without the months it is app.shell.collection_items.

app.photos.grid.empty_collection_text.text: Select photos in Images, then choose Add to collection.
app.photos.grid.empty_collection_text.note: Under the heading This collection is empty. Add to collection is the name of the selection bar's item (app.shell.add_to_collection) and Images the photo section (app.shell.section_images): use the same words. The same sentence as app.shell.collections_empty_text, without the bold. A Go to Images button follows.

app.photos.grid.empty_collection_title.note: Heading in the place of the photos when the collection open in Images has none.

app.photos.grid.no_match_in.note: Under the heading No photos match, while a collection is open in Images. {name} is the collection's name. Write the quotes in your language's style. A Clear search button follows.

app.photos.grid.no_match_text.text: Try other words, or fewer of them.
app.photos.grid.no_match_text.note: Under the heading No photos match, in Images. A Clear search button follows.

app.photos.grid.no_match_title.note: Heading in the place of the photos in Images when no photo matches the search.

app.photos.grid.no_photos_text.text: Photos from the phone and computer apps appear here.
app.photos.grid.no_photos_text.note: Under the heading No photos yet, in Images: photos uploaded by the phone apps and the computer apps of Off The Cloud show here.

app.photos.grid.no_photos_title.note: Heading in the place of the photos in Images when the device has none.

app.photos.grid.people_more.note: Heading over the photos in Images while three or more people are searched for (photos showing all of them). {first} and {second} are the first two names (or app.shell.search_unnamed), {count} how many more people there are.

app.photos.grid.people_two.note: Heading over the photos in Images while two people are searched for (photos showing both of them). {first} and {second} are their names (or app.shell.search_unnamed). Keep it short: it is a heading.

app.photos.grid.person_items.note: Under the names of the people searched for, over their photos in Images: how many photos and videos show them.

app.photos.grid.tile_photo.note: Screen-reader name of a photo's tile in Images when the photo has no date.

app.photos.grid.tile_photo_on.note: Screen-reader name of a photo's tile in Images: the day it was taken. {date} is app.photos.months.day (5 October 2026).

app.photos.grid.tile_video.note: Screen-reader name of a video's tile in Images when the video has no date.

app.photos.grid.tile_video_on.note: Screen-reader name of a video's tile in Images: the day it was taken. {date} is app.photos.months.day (5 October 2026).

app.photos.memories.day_month.note: A day without its year, short (27 Oct), for the days an opened weekly memory covers (app.photos.memories.week_in_year). {day} is the day of the month (1 to 31), {month} the month's short name (app.photos.months.january_short...).

app.photos.memories.hidden.note: Short message at the bottom of the screen after hiding something from the memories (a photo, a memory, a day or a person), next to app.photos.memories.undo.

app.photos.memories.hide_day.note: In an opened memory's menu: never show photos taken on the day of the photo on screen in any memory again (a sad day, for example). The photos themselves stay in Images.

app.photos.memories.hide_failed.note: Short message at the bottom of the screen when hiding something from the memories (a photo, a memory, a day or a person), or undoing it, failed: the device didn't answer. A device that refuses says why in its own words instead.

app.photos.memories.hide_memory.note: In an opened memory's menu: hide this whole memory (this year's photos for this date). The photos themselves stay in Images.

app.photos.memories.hide_person.note: In an opened memory's menu, once for each named person in it: never show photos with this person in any memory again. {name} is the name the user gave the person in People. The photos themselves stay in Images.

app.photos.memories.hide_photo.note: In an opened memory's menu: never show the photo on screen in a memory again. The photo itself stays in Images.

app.photos.memories.next_photo.note: What screen readers offer on an opened memory's slideshow: go to its next photo (tapping the right side of the screen).

app.photos.memories.options.note: What screen readers read for the menu button on an opened memory (a … icon): it holds the ways to hide what shows in the memories.

app.photos.memories.period_day.note: One of three short choices beside the memories strip's title (Day, Week, Month): show the memories of today's date in earlier years.

app.photos.memories.period_month.note: One of three short choices beside the memories strip's title (Day, Week, Month): show the memories of this calendar month in earlier years.

app.photos.memories.period_week.note: One of three short choices beside the memories strip's title (Day, Week, Month): show the memories of the week around today's date in earlier years.

app.photos.memories.photo_position.note: What screen readers read for an opened memory's slideshow: which of its photos is on screen. {index} is its position (from 1), {count} how many photos the memory shows.

app.photos.memories.previous_photo.note: What screen readers offer on an opened memory's slideshow: go back to its previous photo (tapping the left side of the screen).

app.photos.memories.see_all.note: Button on an opened memory: shows all its photos in a grid, where each opens in the photo viewer.

app.photos.memories.title_day.note: Title of the strip of memories at the top of Images, and of a memory opened from it, while it shows the photos taken on today's date in earlier years. The feature's name, as the device calls it.

app.photos.memories.title_month.note: Title of the strip of memories at the top of Images while it shows the photos taken in this calendar month in earlier years.

app.photos.memories.title_week.note: Title of the strip of memories at the top of Images while it shows the photos taken in the week around today's date (three days before to three days after) in earlier years.

app.photos.memories.undo.note: Button next to app.photos.memories.hidden: shows what was just hidden in the memories again.

app.photos.memories.week_in_year.note: The days an opened weekly memory covers, in one year (27 Oct – 2 Nov 2023), after how many years ago. {from} and {to} are short days (app.photos.memories.day_month), the first first; {year} the year in four digits.

app.photos.memories.years_ago.note: On a memory's card in the strip at the top of Images, and in its title when opened: how many years ago its photos were taken. {count} is 1 or more.

app.photos.months.april.note: The month April, written in full: in a month's title over its photos in Images (app.photos.months.title) and in the date screen readers read on a photo's tile (app.photos.months.day). Write it as your language does inside a date, with the capital letter it takes there.

app.photos.months.april_short.note: The month April, shortened as calendars shorten it (Apr): where the whole name doesn't fit (a month one photo wide, app.photos.months.short_title), in the bubble of the date slider beside Images, and in the months an open collection spans (app.photos.months.range_in_year).

app.photos.months.august.note: The month August, written in full: in a month's title over its photos in Images (app.photos.months.title) and in the date screen readers read on a photo's tile (app.photos.months.day). Write it as your language does inside a date, with the capital letter it takes there.

app.photos.months.august_short.note: The month August, shortened as calendars shorten it (Aug): where the whole name doesn't fit (a month one photo wide, app.photos.months.short_title), in the bubble of the date slider beside Images, and in the months an open collection spans (app.photos.months.range_in_year).

app.photos.months.day.note: A day as screen readers read it on a photo's tile in Images (5 October 2026), after app.photos.grid.tile_photo_on or tile_video_on. {day} is the day of the month (1 to 31), {month} the month's full name (app.photos.months.january...), {year} the year in four digits.

app.photos.months.december.note: The month December, written in full: in a month's title over its photos in Images (app.photos.months.title) and in the date screen readers read on a photo's tile (app.photos.months.day). Write it as your language does inside a date, with the capital letter it takes there.

app.photos.months.december_short.note: The month December, shortened as calendars shorten it (Dec): where the whole name doesn't fit (a month one photo wide, app.photos.months.short_title), in the bubble of the date slider beside Images, and in the months an open collection spans (app.photos.months.range_in_year).

app.photos.months.february.note: The month February, written in full: in a month's title over its photos in Images (app.photos.months.title) and in the date screen readers read on a photo's tile (app.photos.months.day). Write it as your language does inside a date, with the capital letter it takes there.

app.photos.months.february_short.note: The month February, shortened as calendars shorten it (Feb): where the whole name doesn't fit (a month one photo wide, app.photos.months.short_title), in the bubble of the date slider beside Images, and in the months an open collection spans (app.photos.months.range_in_year).

app.photos.months.january.note: The month January, written in full: in a month's title over its photos in Images (app.photos.months.title) and in the date screen readers read on a photo's tile (app.photos.months.day). Write it as your language does inside a date, with the capital letter it takes there.

app.photos.months.january_short.note: The month January, shortened as calendars shorten it (Jan): where the whole name doesn't fit (a month one photo wide, app.photos.months.short_title), in the bubble of the date slider beside Images, and in the months an open collection spans (app.photos.months.range_in_year).

app.photos.months.july.note: The month July, written in full: in a month's title over its photos in Images (app.photos.months.title) and in the date screen readers read on a photo's tile (app.photos.months.day). Write it as your language does inside a date, with the capital letter it takes there.

app.photos.months.july_short.note: The month July, shortened as calendars shorten it (Jul): where the whole name doesn't fit (a month one photo wide, app.photos.months.short_title), in the bubble of the date slider beside Images, and in the months an open collection spans (app.photos.months.range_in_year).

app.photos.months.june.note: The month June, written in full: in a month's title over its photos in Images (app.photos.months.title) and in the date screen readers read on a photo's tile (app.photos.months.day). Write it as your language does inside a date, with the capital letter it takes there.

app.photos.months.june_short.note: The month June, shortened as calendars shorten it (Jun): where the whole name doesn't fit (a month one photo wide, app.photos.months.short_title), in the bubble of the date slider beside Images, and in the months an open collection spans (app.photos.months.range_in_year).

app.photos.months.march.note: The month March, written in full: in a month's title over its photos in Images (app.photos.months.title) and in the date screen readers read on a photo's tile (app.photos.months.day). Write it as your language does inside a date, with the capital letter it takes there.

app.photos.months.march_short.note: The month March, shortened as calendars shorten it (Mar): where the whole name doesn't fit (a month one photo wide, app.photos.months.short_title), in the bubble of the date slider beside Images, and in the months an open collection spans (app.photos.months.range_in_year).

app.photos.months.may.note: The month May, written in full: in a month's title over its photos in Images (app.photos.months.title) and in the date screen readers read on a photo's tile (app.photos.months.day). Write it as your language does inside a date, with the capital letter it takes there.

app.photos.months.may_short.note: The month May, shortened as calendars shorten it (May): where the whole name doesn't fit (a month one photo wide, app.photos.months.short_title), in the bubble of the date slider beside Images, and in the months an open collection spans (app.photos.months.range_in_year).

app.photos.months.no_date.note: The bubble of the date slider beside Images while it is on the photos that have no date.

app.photos.months.november.note: The month November, written in full: in a month's title over its photos in Images (app.photos.months.title) and in the date screen readers read on a photo's tile (app.photos.months.day). Write it as your language does inside a date, with the capital letter it takes there.

app.photos.months.november_short.note: The month November, shortened as calendars shorten it (Nov): where the whole name doesn't fit (a month one photo wide, app.photos.months.short_title), in the bubble of the date slider beside Images, and in the months an open collection spans (app.photos.months.range_in_year).

app.photos.months.october.note: The month October, written in full: in a month's title over its photos in Images (app.photos.months.title) and in the date screen readers read on a photo's tile (app.photos.months.day). Write it as your language does inside a date, with the capital letter it takes there.

app.photos.months.october_short.note: The month October, shortened as calendars shorten it (Oct): where the whole name doesn't fit (a month one photo wide, app.photos.months.short_title), in the bubble of the date slider beside Images, and in the months an open collection spans (app.photos.months.range_in_year).

app.photos.months.range.note: Under an open collection's name, after how many items it holds: the time its photos span across years. {from} and {to} are each a short month and year (app.photos.months.short_title: Mar 2024 – Oct 2026), the oldest first, or only the years on a narrow screen (2024 – 2026).

app.photos.months.range_in_year.note: Under an open collection's name, after how many items it holds: the months its photos span when they are all from one year (Mar – Oct 2024). {from} and {to} are short month names (app.photos.months.january_short...), the oldest first; {year} the year in four digits.

app.photos.months.september.note: The month September, written in full: in a month's title over its photos in Images (app.photos.months.title) and in the date screen readers read on a photo's tile (app.photos.months.day). Write it as your language does inside a date, with the capital letter it takes there.

app.photos.months.september_short.note: The month September, shortened as calendars shorten it (Sep): where the whole name doesn't fit (a month one photo wide, app.photos.months.short_title), in the bubble of the date slider beside Images, and in the months an open collection spans (app.photos.months.range_in_year).

app.photos.months.short_title.note: A month and its year, short (Mar 2024): the title of a month one photo wide in Images, where the whole title doesn't fit; the bubble of the date slider beside Images; the months an open collection spans (app.photos.months.range). {month} is the month's short name (app.photos.months.january_short...), {year} the year in four digits.

app.photos.months.title.note: Title over a month's photos in Images (photos in date order): {month} is the month's full name (app.photos.months.january...), {year} the year in four digits (2024). Also what screen readers read for it.

app.photos.notice.add_failed.text: Could not add to the collection.
app.photos.notice.add_failed.note: Alert in Images when the device didn't add the selected photos to the chosen collection.

app.photos.notice.added.note: Alert in Images once the selected photos were added to a collection. {name} is the collection's name.

app.photos.notice.create_failed.note: Alert in Images when the device didn't make the new collection from the selected photos.

app.photos.notice.created.note: Alert in Images once a new collection was made from the selected photos. {name} is its name.

text.one: {count} item changed on your device since it was shown, so it wasn't deleted. Check it and try again.
text.other: {count} items changed on your device since they were shown, so they weren't deleted. Check them and try again.

app.photos.notice.delete_changed.note: Alert in Images (or the photo viewer) after deleting several photos or videos when the device refused two or more of them because the file at their path now holds other content (replaced or synced over since the app showed it): the summed-up message for those refusals (a single refusal shows the device's own message instead). Nothing of those was deleted, they stay selected, and the photos are loaded again. An item is a photo or a video. Same text as web.images.delete.changed.

app.photos.notice.delete_collection_fail.note: Alert in Images when the device didn't delete the open collection.

text.one: {count} item wasn't deleted: a copy of it is in an upload-only folder
text.other: {count} items weren't deleted: they have copies in an upload-only folder

app.photos.notice.delete_copy_upload_onl.note: Alert in Images after deleting every copy of several photos or videos when the device refused two or more of them because one of their copies is in a folder set to upload only: the summed-up message for those refusals (a single refusal shows the device's own message instead). Nothing of those was deleted, and they stay selected. An item is a photo or a video. Same text as web.images.delete.copy_upload_only.

app.photos.notice.delete_failed.note: Alert when deleting a photo (the one open in the viewer, or one of the selected ones) failed. {detail} is the device's own explanation (already in the user's language) or the phone's.

app.photos.notice.no_download_link.note: Alert when the device didn't make the link to download the selected photos as a zip (the selection bar's Download).

app.photos.notice.no_share_link.note: Alert when the device didn't make the link to share the selected photos (the selection bar's Share).

app.photos.notice.not_loaded.note: Alert in the full-screen photo viewer when Share or Save is tapped before the photo has loaded.

app.photos.notice.remove_failed.text: Could not remove from the collection.
app.photos.notice.remove_failed.note: Notice over Images when the selected photos couldn't be taken out of the collection (app.shell.remove_from_collection).

app.photos.notice.removed.note: Notice over Images once the selected photos were taken out of a collection (app.shell.remove_from_collection); the photos themselves are kept. {name} is the collection's name. Use this language's quotation marks.

app.photos.notice.rename_failed.note: Alert in Images when the device didn't rename the open collection.

app.photos.notice.save_failed.note: Alert when saving the photo or video open in the viewer to the phone's photo library failed. {detail} is the reason: the phone's system's words, or why the original couldn't be downloaded from the device (the device's own words, already in the user's language, or the phone's).

app.photos.notice.saved.note: Alert once the photo open in the viewer was saved to the phone's own photo library (Photos on an iPhone, the gallery on Android). Keep the check mark.

app.photos.notice.share_failed.note: Alert when sharing the photo open in the viewer, or a link to the selected photos, failed. {detail} is the reason as the phone's system words it (often in the phone's language).

app.photos.people.add_name.note: Item of a face's menu, and the tappable line under a face without a name, on the People page: opens a field to name the person.

app.photos.people.clear_selection.note: Screen-reader name of the × at the start of the bar shown while faces are picked on the People page: unpicks them all.

app.photos.people.delete_failed.text: They couldn't be deleted. Try again.
app.photos.people.delete_failed.note: Error on the People page when the device deleted none of the people asked (two or more).

app.photos.people.delete_many.note: Title of the confirmation asked before deleting the people picked on the People page (two or more). {count} is how many. The explanation is app.photos.people.delete_text. Buttons: Delete and Cancel.

app.photos.people.delete_named.note: Title of the confirmation asked before deleting a person (the People page: a face's menu or the selection bar). {name} is their name. The explanation is app.photos.people.delete_text. Buttons: Delete and Cancel.

app.photos.people.delete_one.note: Title of the confirmation asked before deleting a person without a name (the People page: a face's menu or the selection bar). The explanation is app.photos.people.delete_text. Buttons: Delete and Cancel.

app.photos.people.delete_one_failed.text: This person couldn't be deleted. Try again.
app.photos.people.delete_one_failed.note: Error on the People page when the device didn't delete the one person asked.

text.one: {count} of {total} people couldn't be deleted and is still selected. Try again.
text.other: {count} of {total} people couldn't be deleted and are still selected. Try again.

app.photos.people.delete_partly.note: Error note at the foot of the People page when some of the picked people were deleted and others not: those stay picked, to try again. {count} is how many couldn't be deleted, {total} how many were asked (two or more).

app.photos.people.delete_text.text: Their photos stay; only the faces matched to them are forgotten. This can't be undone, and they'll come back as new people in photos added later.
app.photos.people.delete_text.note: Explanation in the confirmation asked before deleting people on the People page: what deleting a person does (face recognition forgets them; their photos aren't deleted).

app.photos.people.deleted_many.note: Note at the foot of the People page once the picked people were deleted. {count} is how many (two or more).

app.photos.people.deleted_one.note: Note at the foot of the People page once a person was deleted.

app.photos.people.face_label.note: Screen-reader name of a person's face (People page, the merge's choice of faces, search suggestions). {name} is their name (or app.shell.search_unnamed), {count} how many photos show them.

app.photos.people.face_label_unnamed.note: Screen-reader name of the face of a person without a name on the People page. {count} is how many photos show them.

app.photos.people.failed_title.note: Heading of the People page when the list of people couldn't be loaded from the device. Under it app.shell.collections_failed_text, then a Try again button.

app.photos.people.keep.note: Small badge on the face chosen to keep in the merge's box (People page).

app.photos.people.list_more.note: A list of three or more people's names, one name at a time: {first} is a name, {rest} the rest of the list (itself list_more, or list_two for its last two names: Ana, Leo and Rosa).

app.photos.people.list_two.note: A list of two people's names (Ana and Leo), in app.photos.people.merge_drops_names; also the end of a longer list (app.photos.people.list_more).

app.photos.people.loading.note: Screen-reader name of the grey placeholder faces on the People page while the people load.

app.photos.people.merge.note: Item of the bar shown while faces are picked on the People page, and the confirming button of the merge (app.photos.people.merge_title): makes the picked faces one person (face recognition split one person in several).

app.photos.people.merge_called.text: The merged person will be called {name}.
app.photos.people.merge_called.note: In the merge's box (People page), under the faces: the name the merged person keeps. {name} is that name, in bold (…).

app.photos.people.merge_drops_name.note: In the merge's box (People page), after app.photos.people.merge_called when one of the merged people had another name, which goes. {name} is that name.

app.photos.people.merge_drops_names.note: In the merge's box (People page), after app.photos.people.merge_called when several of the merged people had other names, which go. {names} is the list of those names (app.photos.people.list_two and list_more).

app.photos.people.merge_failed.text: They couldn't be merged. Try again.
app.photos.people.merge_failed.note: Error in the merge's box (People page) when the device didn't merge the picked faces.

app.photos.people.merge_hint.text: Select the faces of the same person
app.photos.people.merge_hint.note: Hint shown with the bar of picked faces on the People page after a face's Merge with others…, until a second face is picked.

app.photos.people.merge_name_label.note: Label over the name field in the merge's box (People page), when the merged person has no name yet. <dim>…</dim> is shown in grey: the name may be left empty.

app.photos.people.merge_name_not_saved.text: The name couldn't be saved, so nothing was merged. Try again.
app.photos.people.merge_name_not_saved.note: Error in the merge's box (People page) when the device didn't give the kept face its name: the merge was not sent.

app.photos.people.merge_name_placeholder.note: Placeholder of the name field in the merge's box (People page), when the merged person has no name yet.

app.photos.people.merge_need_two.text: Select 2 or more faces to merge them into one.
app.photos.people.merge_need_two.note: Note at the foot of the People page when Merge is tapped with only one face picked.

app.photos.people.merge_pick.text: They have different names, and only one can stay. Pick the face to keep.
app.photos.people.merge_pick.note: In the merge's box (People page), under the faces, when the people picked have different names and none is chosen yet.

app.photos.people.merge_text.text: Pick the face to keep: it keeps its name and picture, and gets the photos of the others. This can't be undone.
app.photos.people.merge_text.note: Under the title of the merge's box (People page), over the faces to choose from.

app.photos.people.merge_title.note: Title of the box that merges the faces picked on the People page into one person. {count} is how many (two or more). Merging can't be undone (app.photos.people.merge_text).

app.photos.people.merge_with_others.note: Item of a face's menu on the People page: starts picking the other faces of the same person, to merge them into one.

app.photos.people.merged_faces.note: Note at the foot of the People page once faces were merged into one person without a name. {count} is how many faces were merged (two or more).

app.photos.people.merged_into.note: Note at the foot of the People page once faces were merged into one person. {count} is how many faces were merged (two or more), {name} the merged person's name.

app.photos.people.more_options.note: Screen-reader name of the … button on a face on the People page (its menu: rename, merge, delete). {name} is the person's name.

app.photos.people.more_options_unnamed.note: Screen-reader name of the … button on the face of a person without a name on the People page (its menu: add a name, merge, delete).

app.photos.people.name_not_saved.text: The name couldn't be saved. Try again.
app.photos.people.name_not_saved.note: Error note at the foot of the People page when the device didn't save a person's new name.

app.photos.people.name_placeholder.note: Placeholder of the field that names a person on the People page.

app.photos.people.name_this_person.note: Naming a person without a name on the People page: the title of the box with the name field (Android), or the screen-reader name of the field (iPhone).

app.photos.people.no_answer.text: Your device didn't answer. Try again.
app.photos.people.no_answer.note: Error on the People page (in the merge's or the deletion's box) when the device didn't answer at all.

app.photos.people.no_faces_text.text: Face recognition runs on the device after photos are uploaded. You can switch it on in Settings.
app.photos.people.no_faces_text.note: Under the heading No faces found yet, on the People page. Says where face recognition runs (on the user's own device, never elsewhere) and that it can be turned on in the app's Settings (common.settings).

app.photos.people.no_faces_title.note: Heading of the People page when face recognition hasn't found anyone.

app.photos.people.photo_count.note: Under a person's face on the People page, in the merge's choice of faces and in the search suggestions: how many photos show them (face recognition).

app.photos.people.slow_text.text: People are taking longer than usual to load.
app.photos.people.slow_text.note: Under the heading Still waiting for your device (app.shell.collections_slow_title), on the People page after 10 seconds without an answer; a Try again button follows.

app.photos.people.sort_name.note: In People's Sort by menu: by name, A to Z; people without a name come last.

app.photos.people.sort_photos.note: In People's Sort by menu: the people with the most photos first (the order the device gives, and the default).

app.photos.person.move_failed.note: Error at the foot of Images when the device didn't move the selected photos to the person picked (app.shell.move_to_person).

app.photos.person.move_none.text: No one else has been found yet.
app.photos.person.move_none.note: In the list opened by Someone else… (app.shell.move_to_person) when face recognition has found no other person to move the photos to.

app.photos.person.move_title.note: Title of the list of people opened by Someone else… (app.shell.move_to_person): the faces found by face recognition, with their names; picking one files the selected photos under that person instead. {count} is how many photos are selected.

app.photos.person.moved.note: Note at the foot of Images once photos were moved to another person (app.shell.move_to_person). {count} is how many, {name} the name of the person they went to.

text.one: Moved {count} photo to an unnamed person
text.other: Moved {count} photos to an unnamed person

app.photos.person.moved_unnamed.note: app.photos.person.moved when the person the photos went to has no name yet. {count} is how many photos.

app.photos.person.needs_update.text: Your device needs an update to change who is in a photo.
app.photos.person.needs_update.note: Title of the message shown when Not this person or Someone else… (app.shell.not_this_person, app.shell.move_to_person) is tapped and the device's software is older than that feature. The account that set the device up gets an Update button under it (common.update); others get app.shell.device_update.ask_owner.

app.photos.person.remove_failed.note: Error at the foot of Images (or in the confirmation) when the device didn't take the selected photos off the person (app.shell.not_this_person).

app.photos.person.remove_text.text: The photos stay on your device, and face recognition won't put them back.
app.photos.person.remove_text.note: Explanation in the confirmation of Not this person (app.photos.person.remove_title): the photos aren't deleted, and face recognition won't match them to this person (or anyone) again.

app.photos.person.remove_title.note: Title of the confirmation asked after Not this person (app.shell.not_this_person) among a person's photos. {name} is the person's name, {count} how many photos are selected. The explanation is app.photos.person.remove_text. Buttons: Remove (common.remove) and Cancel.

text.one: Remove this photo from this person?

app.photos.person.remove_title_unnamed.note: app.photos.person.remove_title for a person without a name. {count} is how many photos are selected.

app.photos.person.removed.note: Note at the foot of Images once photos were taken off a person (app.shell.not_this_person). {count} is how many, {name} the person's name.

app.photos.person.removed_unnamed.note: app.photos.person.removed for a person without a name. {count} is how many photos.

app.photos.places.area_chip.note: Chip over the grid in Images once a group of photos on the map was opened: the grid shows only the photos and videos taken in that area of the map. Tapping it shows the map again; its × shows the photos of every place again (app.photos.places.close_area).

app.photos.places.back_to_map.note: Button at the top of Images when it shows the photos of a place opened from the Places map, going back to the map where it was; also the screen-reader hint of the Map area chip (app.photos.places.area_chip), which does the same.

app.photos.places.close_area.note: Screen-reader name of the × on the Map area chip (app.photos.places.area_chip): the grid shows every photo again, not only those taken in that area.

app.photos.places.failed.text: Couldn't load the photos on the map
app.photos.places.failed.note: Small banner over the map (Places) while the device hasn't answered for the photos to draw there. They are asked for again by themselves; the banner's button is common.try_again.

app.photos.places.none.text: No photos with a location yet
app.photos.places.none.note: Over the map in Images (Places) when no photo or video has a position: a phone records one when the camera may use the location.

app.photos.places.none_filtered.text: None of these photos has a location
app.photos.places.none_filtered.note: Over the map in Images (Places) when a search, a person or a collection is picked and none of the photos and videos it shows has a position.

app.photos.places.pin.note: Screen-reader name of a group of photos on the map (Places): a round thumbnail with a count, drawn at the place they were taken. {count} is how many photos and videos it holds, always 2 or more (a single photo is read as app.photos.grid.tile_photo_on). Tapping it zooms in, or opens them in Images.

app.photos.places.reading.text: Finding where your photos were taken…
app.photos.places.reading.note: Small note on the map in Images (Places) while the device is still reading, in the background, where the photos it already held were taken, just after Places was turned on: some photos aren't on the map yet.

app.photos.places.show_grid.note: Screen-reader name of the same button (app.photos.places.show_map) while the map shows: back to the grid of photos.

app.photos.places.show_map.note: Screen-reader name of the button at the top of Images on a narrow phone screen, next to the People and Collections buttons: shows the photos and videos on a map, at the places they were taken, in place of the grid of photos.

app.photos.search.already.note: Under the search field when the thing typed is already a chip in it. {text} is what was typed. Write the quotes in your language's style.

app.photos.search.documents.note: Row in the search suggestions that lists, in Files, every file and folder whose path contains what was typed. {text} is the typed text, in bold (…). Write the quotes in your language's style.

app.photos.search.files.note: Heading of the search suggestions that are files and folders whose name or path matches. Shown in capitals.

app.photos.search.nothing.note: Under the search field when nothing matches what was typed. {text} is what was typed. Write the quotes in your language's style.

app.photos.search.people.note: Heading of the search suggestions that are people found by face recognition. Shown in capitals.

app.photos.search.things.note: Heading of the search suggestions that are things recognised in photos (tags such as beach or dog). Shown in capitals.

app.photos.selection.delete_title.note: Title of the confirmation asked before deleting the selected photos and videos from the device (the selection bar's Delete). {count} is how many are selected. Buttons: Delete and Cancel.

app.photos.smart_search.failed.text: Smart search isn't available right now.
app.photos.smart_search.failed.note: Message when a Smart search (a description typed in the search) can't be done and the device gave no words of its own (it was turned off on another app, or the device can't do it).

app.photos.smart_search.reading.text: Your device is still getting to know your photos…
app.photos.smart_search.reading.note: Quiet note over the photos found by a Smart search (a description typed in the search) while the device is still working out what the photos it already held show, just after Smart search was turned on: some photos may be missing for now.

app.photos.smart_search.search_for.note: Row of the search's suggestions while Smart search is on: finds the photos that best match what was typed, as a description ("kids in the snow"), within the chips already in the search. {text} is what was typed. Write the quotes in your language's style, as app.photos.search.documents.

app.photos.sort_by.note: Title of the menu that picks the order of the People and Collections pages.

app.photos.viewer.delete.note: Confirming button of app.photos.viewer.delete_title: deletes the photo open in the viewer from the device. Title Case in English buttons. A video has its own: app.photos.viewer.delete_video.

app.photos.viewer.delete_title.note: Title of the confirmation asked before deleting the photo open in the full-screen viewer (Images, or a photo opened from Files) from the device. Buttons: Delete Photo and Cancel. A video has its own: app.photos.viewer.delete_video_title.

app.photos.viewer.delete_video.note: Confirming button of app.photos.viewer.delete_video_title: deletes the video open in the viewer from the device. Title Case in English buttons. The video form of app.photos.viewer.delete.

app.photos.viewer.delete_video_title.note: Title of the confirmation asked before deleting the video open in the full-screen viewer (Images, or a video opened from Files) from the device. Buttons: Delete Video and Cancel. The video form of app.photos.viewer.delete_title; the web says the same (web.images.viewer.delete_video_title).

app.photos.viewer.info_aperture.note: Label of a row in the panel with a photo's camera details (app.photos.viewer.info_title): the aperture (f/1.8).

app.photos.viewer.info_camera.note: Label of a row in the panel with a photo's camera details (app.photos.viewer.info_title): the make and model of the camera or phone that took it.

app.photos.viewer.info_dimensions.note: Label of a row in the panel with a photo's camera details (app.photos.viewer.info_title): its width × height in pixels.

app.photos.viewer.info_exposure.note: Label of a row in the panel with a photo's camera details (app.photos.viewer.info_title): the exposure time (1/250).

app.photos.viewer.info_focal_length.note: Label of a row in the panel with a photo's camera details (app.photos.viewer.info_title): the lens's focal length (26 mm).

app.photos.viewer.info_iso.note: Label of a row in the panel with a photo's camera details (app.photos.viewer.info_title): the ISO sensitivity (100).

app.photos.viewer.info_location.note: Label of a row in the panel with a photo's camera details (app.photos.viewer.info_title): the city and country where it was taken.

app.photos.viewer.info_no_exif.text: No EXIF metadata in this file
app.photos.viewer.info_no_exif.note: In the panel with a photo's camera details when the file has none (no camera, exposure or location). EXIF is the standard name of these details.

app.photos.viewer.info_none.note: In the panel with a photo's camera details when the device couldn't read any.

app.photos.viewer.info_taken.note: Label of a row in the panel with a photo's camera details (app.photos.viewer.info_title): when it was taken (a date and time).

app.photos.viewer.info_title.note: Title of the panel with a photo's camera details (EXIF), opened from the viewer's (i) button. Title Case in English titles.

app.photos.viewer.low_res.note: Small pill on the corner of a photo open in the viewer while only its preview is shown (the full photo is loading, or couldn't be loaded).

app.photos.viewer.more_info.note: Screen-reader name of the (i) button of the full-screen photo viewer: shows the photo's camera details (app.photos.viewer.info_title).

app.photos.viewer.saving.note: Screen-reader name of the viewer's Save button while it shows a spinner: the original photo or video is being downloaded from the device and saved to the phone's own photo library (Photos on an iPhone, the gallery on Android).

app.photos.wallpaper.empty.text: This collection has no photos to show.
app.photos.wallpaper.empty.note: In the wallpaper box when the collection has no photos (empty, or only videos): there is nothing to use as wallpaper.

app.photos.wallpaper.failed.text: Couldn't store the photos. Try again.
app.photos.wallpaper.failed.note: Error when the copies for the wallpaper couldn't be downloaded or saved on the phone.

app.photos.wallpaper.lock_note.text: Anyone who sees your lock screen will see these photos.
app.photos.wallpaper.lock_note.note: In the notice before a collection is used as wallpaper, after app.photos.wallpaper.stored_text: the lock screen shows without unlocking the phone.

app.photos.wallpaper.menu.note: In the menu of the collection open in Images: shows this collection's photos as the phone's wallpaper (Android) or on the iPhone's lock screen and in a home screen widget (iPhone). It opens a box that first says the photos will be stored on the phone (app.photos.wallpaper.stored_title).

app.photos.wallpaper.menu_on.note: app.photos.wallpaper.menu once the collection open in Images is already shown as wallpaper: opens its settings, where it can also be stopped.

app.photos.wallpaper.progress.note: Progress while the copies for the wallpaper are downloaded to the phone. {done} is how many are stored so far, {total} how many there are.

app.photos.wallpaper.stopped.text: Stopped. The copies stored on this phone were deleted.
app.photos.wallpaper.stopped.note: Note once a collection is no longer used as wallpaper: the copies of its photos were deleted from the phone (the photos on the user's own device are untouched).

text.one: To show it as your wallpaper, a copy of the photo in “{name}” is saved on this phone, sized for its screen. It stays there until you stop using the collection as wallpaper.
text.other: To show them as your wallpaper, copies of {count} photos from “{name}” are saved on this phone, sized for its screen. They stay there until you stop using the collection as wallpaper.

app.photos.wallpaper.stored_text.note: Under app.photos.wallpaper.stored_title: what is stored and for how long. {count} is how many photos will be copied to the phone (the collection's photos, at most the app's limit), {name} the collection's name. Use this language's quotation marks.

app.photos.wallpaper.stored_title.text: These photos will be stored on this phone
app.photos.wallpaper.stored_title.note: Heading of the notice shown before a collection is used as wallpaper (app.photos.wallpaper.menu), in bold, before anything is stored: copies of the photos will be saved on the phone itself, not only on the user's own device at home. Must be unmistakable.

app.photos.wallpaper.wifi_only.text: Photos download only on Wi-Fi, as “Wi-Fi only” is on in Settings.
app.photos.wallpaper.wifi_only.note: In the wallpaper box while the app's Wi-Fi only setting (app.settings.sync.wifi_only, written the same way) is on: the copies are downloaded only on Wi-Fi. The last word is the app's Settings section (common.settings).
